extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers submitting to Asimov's Science Fiction magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors preparing short fiction, poetry, or borderline speculative pieces for submission to Asimov's Science Fiction magazine, covering editorial mission, content/genre preferences, length, payment, and prohibited material. Useful for shaping manuscripts to the magazine's expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial mission — examine human existence
rubrics_metrics.description: "All fiction should be written to examine or illuminate some aspect of human existence, but in science fiction the backdrop you work against is the size of the Universe."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction should illuminate aspects of human existence; science fiction uses a large/universal backdrop to do so. This sets the magazine's thematic expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-oriented stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters, rather than the science, provide the main focus for the reader's interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should center on character development and human concerns; speculative or scientific elements should serve those character-driven stakes rather than dominate purely as gadgets or technical puzzles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary genre scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction primarily; also borderline fantasy, slipstream, surreal fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asimov's primarily publishes SF but is open to adjacent speculative forms when they fit the magazine's mission. Use genre elements to illuminate human themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited genre — sword & sorcery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional heroic fantasy with swords-and-magic tropes is outside the magazine's preferred scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content — explicit sex or violence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material that is sexually explicit or graphically violent will be rejected; keep content within the magazine's standards for taste and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reprints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only original, unpublished work should be submitted; previously published pieces will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only to Asimov's (or withdraw promptly) while the piece is under consideration; follow their policy to avoid automatic rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-assisted work may be banned
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine indicates concern about AI involvement; authors should avoid or clearly disclose AI assistance and follow current policy, as it may disqualify a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limits for fiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should generally fall within this word-count window; submissions outside these bounds are rarely accepted. Also: no serialized novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: No serialized novels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asimov's will not accept multi-installment novel serializations; submit standalone short fiction or appropriately self-contained pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry length and pay
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems must be 40 lines or fewer to fit the stated pay policy; follow submission instructions for poetry format and length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rates for fiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment terms: stories up to 7,500 words earn 8–10 cents per word; for longer stories the base rate is 8 cents per word for the amount over 7,500. Use these rates to judge commercial fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-centered (not gadget-centered) SF
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The speculative technology or scientific idea should be integrated in service of human concerns; avoid stories that exist mainly to showcase a technical concept without human stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative element must matter to characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative element must matter to characters' lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculation should have clear consequences for characters; the 'what if' must affect motivations, choices, relationships, or psychological states rather than be decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong, clean prose (Asimov's house style)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly and tightly in a readable house style; avoid overwriting, muddled sentences, or overly ornate language that obscures character and narrative spine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear narrative spine even in experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear narrative spine even in literary/surreal experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental, literary, or surreal pieces still need an intelligible through-line or narrative structure so readers can follow emotional or thematic movement.
